This decision was made after assessing current conditions and the outlook for economic activity, the labor market, and inflation. Eight members voted in favor, while one member, Neel Kashkari, dissented. Kashkari preferred to maintain the existing target range, citing concerns about achieving the Committee's 2 percent longer-run inflation objective and the potential for inflation expectations to decline if the rate was raised too soon. cases.answer: Participants noted that while recent data on spending had been strong, driven by a robust job market and rising incomes, there were concerns about the recent softening in consumer surveys regarding spending intentions. They also pointed out that average hourly earnings had increased steadily, with a 3.2% rise over the year, and wage costs, as measured by the Employment Cost Index, had also risen by 3.0% over the year. However, no explicit discussion about wage-price flexibility or inflation expectations was found in the minutes.

Participants noted that the U.S. dollar had fallen back somewhat over the intermeeting period, but it had increased significantly since the middle of last year and was expected to continue restraining U.S. economic activity (a search of the minutes, [2015-04-29/participantsViews/5]). This trend was also observed in 2014, with the dollar appreciating against the euro, yen, and pound sterling (a search of the minutes, [2014-09-17/participantsViews/9]). The broad U.S. dollar index had risen to 105.8 on 2015-05-22, up from 105.5 three months earlier and 93.69 a year earlier (the data, the broad U.S. dollar index).

Participants generally noted that banking stresses had receded and conditions in the banking sector had improved since early March (a search of the minutes returned [2023-06-14/participantsViews/4]). They agreed that a tightening in credit conditions due to banking-sector stress earlier in the year would likely weigh on economic activity, but the extent remained uncertain. Later meetings, including the most recent one on 2023-07-26, also mentioned sound and resilient U.S. banking system conditions.
